sources.title: University of Washington, ME 544, Large-Eddy Simulation lecture notes, 8 May 2018 (29-page PDF)
sources.locator: Complete relevant sections inspected: §3 'Filtering the equations of motion', printed pp. 10–12, Eqs. (16)–(24), and §4 'Models for tau^r_ij', printed pp. 13–15, especially Eq. (30); §5 dynamic-model/backscatter caveats, printed pp. 19–20.

contents.name: §3 exact residual stress, isotropic subgrid-energy part, and modified pressure, printed pp. 10–11, Eqs. (16)–(20)
contents.support: The notes define the exact filtered residual stress, split its trace as 2 k_sgs/3 times the identity in three dimensions, and retain the deviatoric residual in the filtered momentum equation. The item adopts the corresponding 3D isotropic term but does not claim model stress equals the exact covariance.

contents.name: §3 resolved kinetic-energy equation and local backscatter qualification, printed p. 12, Eq. (24)
contents.support: The notes identify the exact stress contraction's role in resolved energy and state that local backscatter is possible for the exact residual stress. This supports keeping the exact transfer separate from the modeled transfer.

contents.name: §4 Smagorinsky eddy-viscosity stress and its modeled transfer sign, printed p. 14, Eq. (30)
contents.support: For the stated 3D deviatoric convention the notes use tau^r_ij = -2 nu_sgs Sbar_ij, with nonnegative original-model nu_sgs, and compute transfer 2 nu_sgs Sbar_ij Sbar_ij >= 0. This is the adopted model-form/sign analogue, not proof of physical adequacy.

contents.name: §5 dynamic-model coefficient and backscatter discussion, printed pp. 19–20
contents.support: The notes distinguish the fixed nonnegative eddy-viscosity model from dynamic models that can have locally negative coefficients and warn that those coefficients do not simply encode measured backscatter. This supports the explicit limitation to the adopted closure only.

sources.title: Jeremy A. Gibbs, LES of Turbulent Flows: Lecture 12, University of Utah, Fall 2016 (26-page PDF)
sources.locator: Complete 26-page lecture inspected; relevant pages 7–8 give the deviatoric stress formula; pp. 17–24 develop its momentum and energy role and its no-backscatter limitation.

contents.name: Eddy-viscosity model class and deviatoric stress, printed pp. 7–8
contents.support: The notes state tau_ij - tau_kk delta_ij/3 = -2 nu_T Sbar_ij with Sbar the symmetric filtered velocity gradient. This independently supports the adopted 3D stress-form closure; the isotropic trace term is stated separately in the postulate.

contents.name: Filtered momentum equation, eddy-viscosity substitution, and resolved energy removal, printed pp. 17–23
contents.support: The notes use the same exact residual-stress sign convention as this run and show that a nonnegative eddy viscosity adds a nonnegative dissipative term to the resolved-scale equation. The local item independently proves the contraction identity.

contents.name: Eddy-viscosity models only represent mean forward transfer and omit instantaneous backscatter, printed p. 23
contents.support: This limitation is reflected in the statement: the theorem concerns the adopted modeled stress and asserts no sign for exact filtered transfer.

sources.title: Glenn Flierl and Raffaele Ferrari, MIT OpenCourseWare 12.820, Turbulence in the Ocean and Atmosphere, Chapter 3 (11-page PDF)
sources.locator: Complete 11-page Chapter 3 PDF inspected; §§3.6–3.8, printed pp. 9–11, closure problem, Reynolds equations, and eddy-viscosity discussion.

contents.name: §3.6 closure problem and need for extra physical assumptions, printed pp. 9–10
contents.support: The notes explain that the nonlinear average produces unclosed correlations and that closure adds physical assumptions not deducible from the motion equations. They support the postulate's explicit adopted-model status, not the exact LES formula.

contents.name: §§3.7–3.8 Reynolds-stress closure and limitations, printed pp. 10–11
contents.support: This is a Reynolds-averaged context rather than the LES filtered stress used here. It is used only to support the modeling-versus-deduction distinction and the warning that simple eddy-viscosity forms are not universal.
